plain_english: So if one of those critics who attack philosophy were to say what they always say: "Why don't you live as boldly as you talk? Why do you watch your words around powerful people? Why do you think money is necessary? Why do you get upset when you lose something, or cry when your wife or friend dies? Why do you care about your reputation and get annoyed by gossip? Why is your estate fancier than it needs to be? Why don't you eat simple meals like you preach? Why is your furniture nicer than necessary? Why do you drink wine older than you are? Why do you have fancy gardens?
original_excerpt: If, therefore, any one of those dogs who yelp at philosophy were to say, as they are wont to do, "Why, then, do you talk so much more bravely than you live? why do you check your words in the presence of your superiors, and consider money to be a necessary implement? why are you disturbed when you sustain losses, and weep on hearing of the death of your wife or your friend? why do you pay regard to common rumour, and feel annoyed by calumnious gossip? why is your estate more elaborately kept than its natural use requires? why do you not dine according to your own maxims? why is your furniture smarter than it need be? why do you drink wine that is older than yourself? why are your grounds laid out?

plain_english: Why do you plant trees that only give shade? Why does your wife wear earrings worth more than a rich man's house? Why do your children wear expensive clothes to school? Why do you need an expert just to serve you dinner? Why isn't your silverware just placed anywhere, but carefully arranged in perfect order with a special person in charge of carving the meat? Add these questions too: Why do you own property overseas? Why do you own more than you can even keep track of? You should be ashamed that you don't recognize your own slaves. Either you're careless because you only have a few, or you're wasteful because you have too many to remember.
original_excerpt: why do you plant trees which afford nothing except shade? why does your wife wear in her ears the price of a rich man's house? why are your children at school dressed in costly clothes? why is it a science to wait upon you at table? why is your silver plate not set down anyhow or at random, but skilfully disposed in regular order, with a superintendent to preside over the carving of the viands?" Add to this, if you like, the questions "Why do you own property beyond the seas? why do you own more than you know of? it is a shame to you not to know your slaves by sight: for you must be very neglectful of them if you only own a few, or very extravagant if you have too many for your memory to retain."

plain_english: I'll criticize myself more harshly later — I'll bring up more faults than you can even think of. But for now, here's my answer: "I'm not a wise man, and I won't pretend to be one just to spite you. So don't expect me to match the greatest people who ever lived. Just expect me to be better than the worst. I'm happy if each day I drop some bad habit and fix some flaw. I haven't reached perfect mental health, and I never will. I treat my spiritual problems like gout — I find ways to ease the pain rather than cure it completely. I'm satisfied if the attacks come less often and hurt less. Compared to your crippled feet, I'm a runner." I'm not saying this to defend myself — I'm drowning in every kind of vice. I'm speaking for someone who has made real progress toward virtue.
original_excerpt: I will add some reproaches afterwards, and will bring more accusations against myself than you think of: for the present I will make you the following answer. "I am not a wise man, and I will not be one in order to feed your spite: so do not require me to be on a level with the best of men, but merely to be better than the worst: I am satisfied, if every day I take away something from my vices and correct my faults. I have not arrived at perfect soundness of mind, indeed, I never shall arrive at it: I compound palliatives rather than remedies for my gout, and am satisfied if it comes at rarer intervals and does not shoot so painfully. Compared with your feet, which are lame, I am a racer." I make this speech, not on my own behalf, for I am steeped in vices of every kind, but on behalf of one who has made some progress in virtue.
